subject: tech
title: What Is a Computer?
about: What a computer is: a machine that follows the instructions people give it, the kinds he sees every day (laptop, desktop, tablet, phone, game console, smartwatch, even a tiny board computer), the small computers hiding inside a calculator and a traffic light, and why a block or a book is not one. NC K2-CS-01 (choosing devices for a task) and K2-CS-02 (naming computer parts). Read it together: the tablet reads every card aloud, and you add the stories from your own house.
tip: Walk through the house together and point: computer or not a computer? Ask him how he can tell.

cards.q: A computer is a machine. What does it do?
cards.note: A computer is a machine that follows the instructions people give it, step by step.

cards.q: A computer that folds shut and sits on your lap. What is it called?
cards.note: A laptop is a computer you can carry. The screen folds down over the keys like a book closing.

cards.q: A big computer that stays on a desk with its own screen. What is it called?
cards.note: A desktop computer stays in one place. Its screen, keyboard and mouse are separate parts.

cards.q: A flat computer you hold in your hands and tap with a finger. What is it?
cards.note: A tablet is a computer. The whole front is a touch screen, so you tap instead of typing.

cards.q: A small computer that fits in a pocket and makes calls. Which kind is that?
cards.note: A phone is a tiny computer. It can call, take photos, play music and play games.

cards.q: What do you call the computer box that plays games on the TV?
cards.note: A game console is a computer made just for games. The TV is its screen and the controller is how you talk to it.

cards.q: A tiny computer you wear on your wrist. What do people call it?
cards.note: A smartwatch tells the time and counts your steps. It is a computer small enough to wear.

cards.q: Some computers are little boards as small as a cracker. What do you plug in to use one?
cards.note: A little board computer works like a big one. Plug in a screen and a keyboard and it is ready to go.
A block and a ball cannot follow instructions. A tablet can, so it is a computer.

cards.q: What is inside a paper book?
cards.note: A paper book is not a computer. It has no chip and needs no electricity, just your eyes.

cards.q: What is hiding inside a calculator?
cards.note: A calculator has a tiny computer chip inside. The chip does the math and shows the answer.

cards.q: What tells a traffic light when to turn red or green?
cards.note: A tiny computer inside the traffic light counts the seconds and changes the light.

cards.q: What does every computer need to turn on?
cards.note: Electricity comes from a plug in the wall or from a battery. No power, no computer.
People design computers and build them in factories. Computers do not grow on their own.

cards.q: Who tells a computer what to do?
cards.note: A computer waits for a person to tap, type or program it. Then it does exactly that.

cards.q: A computer adds a hundred numbers in a blink. What is a computer very good at?
cards.note: Computers are super fast at math and at finding things. That is why people use them.

cards.q: Who has feelings and ideas of their own, you or a computer?
cards.note: A computer has no feelings and no ideas of its own. It only follows instructions. Your ideas are yours.

cards.q: What do we call the steps a person gives a computer to follow?
cards.note: Instructions tell a computer what to do, step by step. A list of them is called a program.
